To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
p300 and/or CBP are necessary for photoreceptor-specific chromatin organization and gene expression.
transcriptional coactivators p 300 and CBP are necessary for photoreceptor-specific chromatin organization and gene expression.
p300 and/or CBP are required for the maintenance of photoreceptor-specific gene expression and chromatin organization.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the mechanisms of transcriptional regulation of photoreceptor-specific genes.
the role of p300 and CBp in the regulation of gene expression in the developing photoreceptor cells.
the role of transcription factors and coactivators in the development and differentiation of rod and cone photoreceptors in the retina.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the transcription coactivators CBP and p300 are necessary for photoreceptor-specific chromatin organization and gene expression.

both CBP and p300 play a crucial role in the differentiation of photoreceptor cells and that their loss results in severe disruption in the differentiation process and that this disruption is more severe in the absence of both factors than either one alone.
the p300/CBP coactivators are necessary for the establishment of photoreceptor-specific chromatin organization and expression of photoreceptor genes.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
p300 and Cbp are essential for the maintenance of photoreceptor cell morphology and function.
both Ep300 and CrebBP are required for photoreceptor-specific chromatin organization and gene expression.
the two histone acetyltransferases p300 and CBp play essential roles in establishing and maintaining photoreceptor identity.
The main takeaway from our work is that
p300 and/or CBP are required for the establishment of the unique photoreceptor nuclear structure, and that this is essential for the proper expression of a specific subset of genes.
both p300 and CBp are required for proper photoreceptor development.
the two transcription coactivators, p300 and CBp, are required for photoreceptor-specific chromatin organization and gene expression.
